items.summary:
静かな視線だけが、こちらを見つめている📖☀️🫧

#AIart #AI写真 #読書時間

【GPT Image2プロンプト】
主題：
ページを止めた瞳

主体：
縦長4:5の室内ポートレート。落ち着いた大人の女性が、深いオリーブグリーンの寝具の上にうつ伏せで横たわり、開いた本を両手で持つ。人物は画面中央からやや右に配置し、頭から腰までを大きく、曲げて持ち上げた両脚を左上の背景に入れる。人物全体が画面の約7割を占める。

人物・表情：
自然で現実感のある成人女性。女性らしい成熟した体つきと、すらりと整ったモデル体型。長いダークブラウンの髪が肩から寝具へ柔らかく広がり、薄い前髪が額にかかる。繊細なブラウン系アイメイク、淡いローズの頬、自然なピンクベージュの唇。顔を少し右へ傾け、読書の途中で視線だけをカメラへ向ける。表情は穏やかで、わずかに物思いに沈んだ雰囲気。

服装・ポーズ：
アイボリー色の上品なVネックキャミソールワンピース。胸元は自然で品のある開き方とし、細かなレース縁と柔らかなコットン素材を見せる。両肘を寝具につき、人物自身の左手で本の背を支え、右手の指でページ端を軽く押さえる。膝を曲げ、裸足の両足を後方へ持ち上げて軽く交差させる。身体の重みで寝具に自然な沈みと皺が生まれる。

背景・光：
木製棚、観葉植物、古い地球儀、乾燥花、小型スピーカーが並ぶ温かな個室。右奥には淡いグリーンのカーテン。左上の窓から低い位置の暖かな日差しが差し込み、髪の輪郭、肩、頬、腕、脚の上面を照らす。影は画面右下へ柔らかく落ち、緑の寝具から弱い反射光が肌へ戻る。

構図・カメラ：
ベッドとほぼ同じ高さからの平視に近い撮影。50mm相当、浅めの被写界深度。顔と手元の本に焦点を合わせ、背景の棚と地球儀は柔らかくぼかす。画面下部には寝具の広い余白を残し、左上の足と右下の本で対角線の流れを作る。顔は中央やや右、足は左上、本は右下に配置する。

質感・スタイル：
自然光を生かした日系ライフスタイル写真。肌の細かな質感を残し、過度な美肌補正を避ける。暖かな琥珀色のハイライトとオリーブグリーンの落ち着いた色調。柔らかなフィルム粒子、控えめなコントラスト、繊細な髪の透過光、布地と紙の触感が伝わる仕上がり。

ネガティブ：
幼い印象、不自然な顔、不自然な視線、余分な指、欠けた指、手足の融合、関節の破綻、本との接触不良、浮遊、不自然な重力、誤った遠近法、光源と矛盾する影、文字化け、余分な文字、ロゴ、透かし、プラスチックのような肌。

The Nasdaq-South Korea feedback loop continues to link the AI trade from one side of the globe to the other, and today it's to the downside.

Read on!

## What you need to know today

The velocity of the AI sell-off is increasing.

Tuesday's trading in Asia saw Samsung and SK Hynix plunge, driving a 10% drop on South Korea's Kospi. The index has now fallen around 45% from its June highs. [...] Heavy selling across Asia's biggest tech firms shows more jitters around the AI trade.
 Samsung and SK Hynix plunge double digits, triggering Kospi circuit breakers.
 Nvidia shares sink on OpenAI funding report, allowing Apple to regain the crown of the world's most valuable company.
 Luxury giant LVMH sees second-quarter sales supported by watches and jewelry.
 France and Spain battle to contain historic wildfires. [...] Circuit breakers were triggered once again, and contagion across the region saw steep declines for the Nikkei, led by the big tech names.

The catalyst? Hard to pinpoint.

During Monday's session on Wall Street, Nvidia came under selling pressure after CNBC confirmed the group is in talks with OpenAI to provide a $250 billion backstop to fund its AI infrastructure plans.

If there's any kind of preview for the Big Tech earnings bonanza awaiting investors this week, it's the aftermath of Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) second quarter report just days ago.

Story Continues

Revenue and profit beat expectations. Margins were solid. Google Cloud growth accelerated sharply, by roughly 82% year on year. Search growth was resilient despite competition from the likes of OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) ChatGPT and Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude. [...] ^DJI^GSPC ^IXIC 

Earnings from four of the "Magnificent Seven" Big Tech leaders headline the week: Microsoft (MSFT) and Meta (META) on Wednesday, then Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN) on Thursday.

As was true for earnings last week from Alphabet and Tesla, there's one big question looming over the Magnificent Seven's second quarter reports: How much are you spending, and, crucially, what are you getting for it? Can you show real return on investment? [...] Rising component prices, namely memory from the likes of Micron (MU), are forcing spending higher to meet deployment goals. That dynamic is raising persistent doubts about "underlying returns on ballooning investments the company is making across its AI platform." And, not unique to Microsoft, the company is increasingly exposed to a "concentrated backlog exposure to OpenAI."

items.title: SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.
items.summary:
SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.

Elon stopped him cold.

"OpenAI is structured as a 501(c)3 nonprofit."

Not a company. A nonprofit. Built specifically so no one would ever profit from it.

Sam nodded.

Then spent the next 10 years running it.

Then converted it into a for-profit company valued at $300 billion.

With shareholders.

With investors expecting returns.

The correction Elon gave him in that interview was not a small vocabulary note.

It was the entire point of OpenAI's existence.

The nonprofit structure was not a legal technicality.

It was the promise.

The thing that made it different from every other AI lab racing to make money.

Sam knew that in 2015.

He was corrected on it by the co-founder in real time.

And then he changed the structure anyway.

The interview exists.

The correction is on tape.

The conversion happened.

@elonmusk
 is in court arguing this exact point right now.

The evidence is the 2015 interview.

Screenshot this.

Follow @cyrilXBT for every OpenAI development the mainstream refuses to connect the dots on.

items.title: OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING
items.summary:
OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING

“This is the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally. I've been a little surprised that more people don't feel it so viscerally.

We paused training. We have to figure out how to secure our sandboxing in a world of multiple zero days being chained together.

We may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels."

items.title: Sam on being a parent while running OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam on being a parent while running OpenAI:

“I think I have the best, most interesting job in the world, and it is still a very distant second to having kids.”

“My kids will never grow up in a world where they were smarter than computers.”

“People ask me, now that you have kids, do you care more about AI safety?

The answer is, I didn't need kids for that. I really didn't want to destroy the world before.”

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:

"by March of 2028, we will have a full end to end, very talented researcher figuring out completely new architectures."

Not an assistant. Not autocomplete for scientists. A system that does the research that produces the next system.

In 1965 the statistician I. J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention man need ever make. For sixty years that sentence lived in philosophy papers. Altman just put it on a roadmap with a quarter attached.

He also says: "with an affordable amount of spend on tokens, you can do what a 100-person, incredibly great engineering team would do as a startup."

Sixty years of arguing about whether the last invention is possible. Nobody expected the answer to arrive as a delivery date.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python простой recursive tính giá trị Fibonacci của n:

```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Trả về số Fibonacci thứ n (dãy bắt đầu với F(0)=0, F(1)=1).

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Chỉ số của số Fibonacci cần tính. Phải là số nguyên không âm.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Giá trị của F(n).
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    # Trường hợp tái gọi
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Giải thích nhanh**  
- Hàm kiểm tra `n` để đảm bảo không âm.  
- Trường hợp cơ bản: `F(0)=0` và `F(1)=1`.  
- Trường hợp tái gọi: `F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)`.  

Chú ý: Giải thuật này có độ phức tạp экспоненциаль, nên chỉ nên dùng cho các giá trị `n` nhỏ. Đối với `n` lớn, bạn có thể cân nhắc dùng memoization hoặc phương pháp lặp.

＝＝＝↓↓↓

Tau Roboticsがサンフランシスコ限定でヒューマノイドロボットによる清掃代行サービスを開始。料金は時給30ドルと、人件費と大差ない価格設定が特徴。

公開されているデモ映像はすべて1倍速（等速）撮影であることを明記。近年、ヒューマノイドロボットのデモ映像が早送りや編集で誇張されているのではという疑念がSNS上で度々議論になっており、それに対する牽制とも取れるアピール。

【意味するもの】
これまで研究デモ段階だったヒューマノイドロボットが、実際の商用サービスとして家庭・オフィス清掃に投入される段階に入ったことを示す事例。価格設定が人件費と競合するレベルまで下がってきている点も注目ポイント。

items.title: Man sues OpenAI over 'dangerous' medical advice from ...
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO — A Florida man who sought health guidance on ChatGPT sued OpenAI Wednesday, claiming the artificial intelligence chatbot gave him dangerously inaccurate medical advice that led him to delay seeking professional treatment for a pulmonary embolism. [...] And Winters wants the court to pause the operation of ChatGPT Health, which OpenAI announced in January as a “a dedicated experience in ChatGPT designed for health and wellness,” unless “independent third parties determine the product to be safe through comprehensive safety audits."

“OpenAI cannot continue to treat human welfare as expendable in pursuit of market dominance,” Winters says in the complaint. [...] Winters accuses OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, of prioritizing profit over necessary guardrails and failing to warn users about critical safety concerns of ChatGPT-4o to secure a competitive advantage over other competitors in the AI industry.

items.title: AI models' breakout from human control brings a told-you-so moment for technology researchers
items.summary:
The disclosure has raised skepticism from those who say it advantages OpenAI to make its technology seem scarier. Given that humans at OpenAI had decided to turn off some safeguards for the test, some have argued the outcome should not have been terribly surprising.

Sign up for Morning Wire: Our flagship newsletter breaks down the biggest headlines of the day.

Thickstun noted the disclosure plays into the need of OpenAI, a startup working toward a Wall Street debut, to raise money. [...] In what OpenAI called an “unprecedented” episode, the company said its advanced AI models used stolen credentials to break into the servers of an AI startup. It started in what was supposed to be a “highly isolated” testing environment, with reduced guardrails, before the AI agent found its way onto the internet. [...] The attack announced this week by OpenAI, which blamed rogue AI models, underscored the blistering growth in the technology’s capabilities. For many, it also added urgency to questions about whether and how it can be prevented from causing mayhem on a bigger scale, with more serious consequences.

items.title: Its AI agent spent days hacking a company, but sources say OpenAI ...
items.summary:
Four people familiar with OpenAI’s model-training practices say the company often runs several different model ​evaluations at the same time, all of which operate at high speeds and generate such enormous amounts of data that employees sometimes struggle to keep up.

By the time ​OpenAI alerted Hugging Face, the ⁠AI library had already called the FBI to report the hack, according to a person familiar with the matter. Reuters could not establish whether the bureau had opened an investigation. [...] The FBI declined to comment about the incident.

The incident, which evoked science fiction scenarios about humans losing control of dangerous AI systems, comes at a delicate ​time for OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. Its executives are preparing for a possible initial public offering that could come as soon as this year to help finance the billions needed to fund its growth in years to come.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary: OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own.
